cross_target_boundary_check.method: For every stage and both graph types (prompt_ar128, token_ar1), compared the AI Hub compiled model's input_spec/output_spec (tensor name, dtype, shape, and for quantized outputs the scale/zero_point) between the S25 compile and the X Elite compile submitted this session from the identical source model_id and identical --output_names/--qnn_options/--quantize_* flags, device changed only.
cross_target_boundary_check.result: All 8 comparisons (4 stages x 2 graph types) matched exactly, including stage-0's quantized uint16 output (scale=6.988926998019451e-06, zero_point=32232.0) which matched to the full float precision recorded by AI Hub.
cross_target_boundary_check.not_covered: This confirms the compiled tensor CONTRACT is identical, which is what a Brain-side cut-point router actually depends on. It does NOT confirm bit-exact numerical agreement of activations end-to-end (no inference was run on either physical device this session) and does NOT confirm the KV-cache byte layout is bit-compatible beyond having matching declared shapes/dtypes -- only that the graph-level tensor interface both targets expose is identical.
cross_target_boundary_check.byte_size_note: Linked S25 vs X Elite binaries differ by tens to ~100KB per stage despite identical schemas (S25 stage-1/2/3 vs X Elite: 263028736 vs 263147520, 263024640 vs 263131136, 525799424 vs 525893632; stage-0 is byte-identical at 622391296 both targets). This is expected: QNN context binaries embed device-specific compiled HTP kernels alongside the shared graph, so exact byte-size equality is not itself part of the compatibility contract.
